stem.text: Twenty million years ago there was an ocean between the continents of North America and South America. The snapping shrimp, Alpheus sp., lived in this ocean.
About 3 million years ago, volcanic activity and sedimentation formed a narrow strip of land, Panama, joining North America and South America.
Figure 4.2 shows the area 20 million years ago and now.

stem.caption: Figure 4.2
stem.alt: Maps of North and South America 20 million years ago and now, showing Panama.

stem.text: Snapping shrimp living in the Caribbean Sea near Panama look similar to snapping shrimp living in the Pacific Ocean near Panama. However, if they are paired together, they do not mate.
Explain how, over time, the snapping shrimp living in the Caribbean Sea and the snapping shrimp living in the Pacific Ocean developed so that they now do not mate with each other.

explanation.text: Formation of a land barrier interrupts gene flow between aquatic populations. Different mutations, genetic drift and selection can accumulate until mating behaviour or other reproductive barriers prevent interbreeding.

reasoningChain: Trace independent genetic change to reproductive isolation.

explanation.text: An ecosystem includes organisms, their physical environment and the interactions between them. A niche concerns the role of a particular species and its relationships and resource use within that system.
